leg-ankle--anterior.name: Anterior leg
leg-ankle--anterior.summary: Dorsiflexors and toe extensors. Supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

leg-ankle--lateral.name: Lateral leg
leg-ankle--lateral.summary: The evertors of the foot. Supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

leg-ankle--superficial-calf.name: Superficial calf
leg-ankle--superficial-calf.summary: The plantarflexors that form the calf and join the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

leg-ankle--deep-calf.name: Deep calf
leg-ankle--deep-calf.summary: Popliteus and the three long muscles that pass behind the medial malleolus (Tom, Dick and Harry: tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus).

foot-area--dorsum.name: Dorsum of the foot
foot-area--dorsum.summary: The two short extensors on the top of the foot.

foot-area--sole-1.name: Sole, first layer
foot-area--sole-1.summary: The most superficial layer, just under the plantar aponeurosis.

foot-area--sole-2.name: Sole, second layer
foot-area--sole-2.summary: Muscles attached to the long flexor tendons.

foot-area--sole-3.name: Sole, third layer
foot-area--sole-3.summary: Short muscles of the big and little toes.

foot-area--sole-4.name: Sole, fourth layer
foot-area--sole-4.summary: The interossei, between the metatarsals. Dorsal interossei abduct and plantar interossei adduct the toes (DAB and PAD).

shoulder--deltoid.name: Deltoid
shoulder--deltoid.summary: The cap of the shoulder, in three parts. All supplied by the axillary nerve.

shoulder--rotator-cuff.name: Rotator cuff
shoulder--rotator-cuff.summary: Four muscles that hold the humeral head in the shallow glenoid: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis (SITS).

shoulder--teres-major.name: Teres major
shoulder--teres-major.summary: Runs from the scapula to the humerus alongside latissimus dorsi. The muscles that move the scapula are in the back and chest wall groups.

arm--anterior.name: Anterior arm
arm--anterior.summary: Elbow flexors. All supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.

arm--posterior.name: Posterior arm
arm--posterior.summary: The three heads of triceps, the elbow extensor. Supplied by the radial nerve.

forearm--anterior-superficial.name: Anterior forearm, superficial
forearm--anterior-superficial.summary: Pronator and wrist flexors arising from the medial epicondyle (the common flexor origin).

forearm--anterior-intermediate.name: Anterior forearm, intermediate
forearm--anterior-intermediate.summary: Flexor digitorum superficialis, which bends the middle joints of the fingers.

forearm--anterior-deep.name: Anterior forearm, deep
forearm--anterior-deep.summary: The deep flexors of the fingers and thumb, and the main pronator.

forearm--posterior-superficial.name: Posterior forearm, superficial
forearm--posterior-superficial.summary: Wrist and finger extensors arising near the lateral epicondyle (the common extensor origin). All supplied by the radial nerve or its deep branch.

forearm--posterior-deep.name: Posterior forearm, deep
forearm--posterior-deep.summary: Supinator and the outcropping thumb muscles, plus the index finger extensor. Supplied by the posterior interosseous nerve.

hand-area--thenar.name: Thenar muscles
hand-area--thenar.summary: The ball of the thumb. Mostly supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

hand-area--hypothenar.name: Hypothenar muscles
hand-area--hypothenar.summary: The ball of the little finger. Supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

hand-area--central.name: Central hand
hand-area--central.summary: Adductor pollicis, the lumbricals and the interossei: the fine movements of the fingers.

back--superficial.name: Superficial back (to the upper limb)
back--superficial.summary: Back muscles that move the scapula and arm rather than the spine. Supplied by anterior rami (and the accessory nerve for trapezius), unlike the true back muscles.

back--intermediate.name: Intermediate back
back--intermediate.summary: Thin respiratory muscles between the spine and the ribs.

back--splenius.name: Splenius
back--splenius.summary: The superficial layer of the true (deep) back muscles, wrapping the back of the neck.

back--erector-spinae.name: Erector spinae
back--erector-spinae.summary: Three columns (iliocostalis laterally, longissimus in the middle, spinalis medially) that extend and side-bend the spine. Supplied by posterior rami.

back--transversospinales.name: Transversospinales
back--transversospinales.summary: Deep muscles running from transverse processes up to spinous processes. They stabilise each segment and rotate the spine toward the opposite side.

back--segmental.name: Segmental muscles
back--segmental.summary: Small muscles between adjacent vertebrae, important for posture sense as much as for movement.

back--suboccipital.name: Suboccipital muscles
back--suboccipital.summary: Four short muscles under the skull that fine-tune head position. Supplied by the suboccipital nerve (C1).

thorax-area--pectoral.name: Pectoral muscles
thorax-area--pectoral.summary: Chest muscles that attach the upper limb to the front of the trunk and move the shoulder and scapula.

thorax-area--wall.name: Thoracic wall
thorax-area--wall.summary: Muscles between and around the ribs that move them during breathing. Supplied by the intercostal nerves.

thorax-area--diaphragm.name: Diaphragm
thorax-area--diaphragm.summary: The dome between chest and abdomen and the main muscle of breathing in.

abdomen--anterolateral.name: Anterolateral abdominal wall
abdomen--anterolateral.summary: Rectus abdominis and the three flat muscles (external oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis). They flex and rotate the trunk and compress the abdomen.

abdomen--posterior.name: Posterior abdominal wall
abdomen--posterior.summary: Quadratus lumborum, beside the lumbar spine. Psoas major and iliacus, the other posterior wall muscles, are under the hip area because they act on the hip.

abdomen--pelvic-floor.name: Pelvic floor
abdomen--pelvic-floor.summary: Levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus) and coccygeus: the muscular floor that supports the pelvic organs.

head--scalp.name: Scalp
head--scalp.summary: Occipitofrontalis and its neighbour, joined by the epicranial aponeurosis. All muscles of facial expression are supplied by the facial nerve (CN VII).

head--eyelids.name: Around the eye
head--eyelids.summary: Muscles that close the eyelids and move the eyebrows.

head--nose.name: Around the nose
head--nose.summary: Small muscles that flare or narrow the nostrils.

head--mouth.name: Around the mouth
head--mouth.summary: The largest group of facial muscles: they open, close and shape the lips and cheeks.

head--mastication.name: Muscles of mastication
head--mastication.summary: The chewing muscles that move the mandible at the temporomandibular joint. All supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3).

head--eye-muscles.name: Eye muscles
head--eye-muscles.summary: Two of the extraocular muscles are in the model. Remember LR6 SO4: lateral rectus by CN VI, superior oblique by CN IV, the rest by CN III.

head--tongue.name: Tongue
head--tongue.summary: Extrinsic tongue muscles, supplied by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

neck--superficial.name: Superficial neck
neck--superficial.summary: Platysma in the skin and sternocleidomastoid, which divides the neck into its anterior and posterior triangles.

neck--suprahyoid.name: Suprahyoid muscles
neck--suprahyoid.summary: Above the hyoid: they raise the hyoid for swallowing or, with the hyoid fixed, open the jaw.

neck--infrahyoid.name: Infrahyoid muscles
neck--infrahyoid.summary: The strap muscles below the hyoid. They pull the hyoid and larynx down; mostly supplied by the ansa cervicalis (C1–C3).

neck--scalenes.name: Scalenes
neck--scalenes.summary: Lateral neck muscles running to the first two ribs. The brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle scalenes.

neck--prevertebral.name: Prevertebral muscles
neck--prevertebral.summary: Deep neck flexors lying on the front of the cervical spine.

gluteus-maximus.origin: Outer ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, the back of the sacrum and coccyx, and the sacrotuberous ligament.
gluteus-maximus.insertion: Most fibres into the iliotibial tract; the deep lower fibres into the gluteal tuberosity of the femur.
gluteus-maximus.actionText: Extends the hip, especially from a flexed position (rising from a chair, climbing stairs), and rotates it laterally. Through the iliotibial tract it helps steady the extended knee.
gluteus-maximus.note: Weak gluteus maximus shows as difficulty rising from sitting and a backward trunk lurch when walking.

gluteus-medius.origin: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines.
gluteus-medius.insertion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter.
gluteus-medius.actionText: Abducts the hip and its anterior fibres rotate it medially. Most importantly, it keeps the pelvis level when the opposite foot is off the ground.
gluteus-medius.note: Weakness gives a positive Trendelenburg sign: the pelvis drops on the unsupported side.

gluteus-minimus.origin: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
gluteus-minimus.insertion: Anterior surface of the greater trochanter.
gluteus-minimus.actionText: Abducts and medially rotates the hip; with gluteus medius it keeps the pelvis level in single-leg stance.

tensor-fasciae-latae.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the front of the iliac crest.
tensor-fasciae-latae.insertion: The iliotibial tract, which attaches to the lateral condyle of the tibia (Gerdy's tubercle).
tensor-fasciae-latae.actionText: Flexes, abducts and medially rotates the hip, and tenses the iliotibial tract to steady the extended knee.

piriformis.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum (roughly S2–S4) and the sacrotuberous ligament.
piriformis.insertion: Upper border of the greater trochanter.
piriformis.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.
piriformis.note: The landmark of the gluteal region: the sciatic nerve usually exits the pelvis just below it.

superior-gemellus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, by blending with the obturator internus tendon.
superior-gemellus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.

obturator-internus.origin: Inner (pelvic) surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around it.
obturator-internus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, after turning around the lesser sciatic notch.
obturator-internus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip, abducts the flexed hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

inferior-gemellus.origin: Upper part of the ischial tuberosity.
inferior-gemellus.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, by blending with the obturator internus tendon.
inferior-gemellus.actionText: Laterally rotates the extended hip and abducts the flexed hip.

quadratus-femoris.origin: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity.
quadratus-femoris.insertion: Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest of the femur.
quadratus-femoris.actionText: Laterally rotates the hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

psoas-major.origin: Sides of the bodies of T12–L5 and the discs between them, and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae.
psoas-major.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, through a tendon shared with iliacus.
psoas-major.actionText: Flexes the hip. With the thigh fixed it flexes the trunk (sitting up from lying) and bends the lumbar spine to the same side.
psoas-major.note: A tight psoas pulls the lumbar spine into extension and the pelvis into anterior tilt.

iliacus.origin: Iliac fossa, inner lip of the iliac crest and the ala of the sacrum.
iliacus.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, through the psoas tendon.
iliacus.actionText: Flexes the hip, and with psoas major flexes the trunk on the fixed thigh.

rectus-femoris.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine (straight head) and the ilium just above the acetabulum (reflected head).
rectus-femoris.insertion: Base of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
rectus-femoris.actionText: Extends the knee and flexes the hip.
rectus-femoris.note: The only quadriceps muscle that crosses the hip, so it is a two-joint muscle.

vastus-lateralis.origin: Greater trochanter, upper intertrochanteric line and the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
vastus-lateralis.originShort: Greater trochanter and lateral linea aspera
vastus-lateralis.insertion: Base and lateral border of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-lateralis.note: The largest part of the quadriceps.

vastus-medialis.origin: Intertrochanteric line and the medial lip of the linea aspera.
vastus-medialis.insertion: Base and medial border of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-medialis.actionText: Extends the knee. Its lowest fibres (often called VMO) pull the patella medially and help it track in the femoral groove.

vastus-intermedius.origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the femoral shaft.
vastus-intermedius.insertion: Base of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
vastus-intermedius.note: Lies deep to rectus femoris, directly on the femur.

sartorius.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
sartorius.actionText: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip, and flexes the knee: together, the cross-legged sitting position.
sartorius.note: The longest muscle in the body.

pectineus.origin: Pectineal line (pecten) of the superior pubic ramus.
pectineus.insertion: Pectineal line of the femur, just below the lesser trochanter.
pectineus.nerveNote: Femoral nerve (sometimes also the obturator nerve)

adductor-longus.origin: Body of the pubis, just below the pubic crest.
adductor-longus.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera.
adductor-longus.actionText: Adducts the hip and helps flex it.
adductor-longus.note: Its tendon is the one most often strained in a groin injury.

adductor-brevis.origin: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
adductor-brevis.originShort: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
adductor-brevis.insertion: Pectineal line and the upper part of the linea aspera.
adductor-brevis.actionText: Adducts the hip and helps flex it.

adductor-magnus.origin: Adductor part: inferior pubic ramus and ischial ramus. Hamstring part: ischial tuberosity.
adductor-magnus.insertion: Adductor part: gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera and medial supracondylar line. Hamstring part: adductor tubercle.
adductor-magnus.nerveNote: Adductor part: obturator nerve. Hamstring part: tibial division of the sciatic nerve
adductor-magnus.actionText: Adducts the hip. The adductor part also flexes it; the hamstring part extends it.
adductor-magnus.note: A muscle with two nerves because it is really two muscles fused together.

adductor-minimus.name: Adductor minimus
adductor-minimus.origin: Inferior pubic ramus (the upper part of adductor magnus).
adductor-minimus.insertion: Upper linea aspera, below the gluteal tuberosity.
adductor-minimus.actionText: Adducts and laterally rotates the hip.
adductor-minimus.note: Often described as the uppermost part of adductor magnus rather than a separate muscle.

gracilis.origin: Body of the pubis and the inferior pubic ramus.
gracilis.originShort: Body and inferior ramus of pubis
gracilis.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
gracilis.actionText: Adducts the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
gracilis.note: The only adductor that crosses the knee.

obturator-externus.origin: Outer surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around the obturator foramen.
obturator-externus.actionText: Laterally rotates the hip and holds the femoral head in the acetabulum.

semitendinosus.insertion: Upper medial surface of the tibia, as part of the pes anserinus.
semitendinosus.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
semitendinosus.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
semitendinosus.note: Its long tendon makes up the lower half of the muscle.

semimembranosus.insertion: Posterior surface of the medial tibial condyle.
semimembranosus.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
semimembranosus.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
semimembranosus.note: Lies deep to semitendinosus. Its flat upper tendon gives it its name.

long-head-of-biceps-femoris.name: Biceps femoris, long head
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.insertion: Lateral side of the head of the fibula.
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.nerveNote: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
long-head-of-biceps-femoris.actionText: Extends the hip, flexes the knee and laterally rotates the leg when the knee is bent.

short-head-of-biceps-femoris.name: Biceps femoris, short head
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.origin: Lateral lip of the linea aspera and the lateral supracondylar line of the femur.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.insertion: Lateral side of the head of the fibula, shared with the long head.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.nerveNote: Common fibular division of the sciatic nerve
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.actionText: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the leg when the knee is bent.
short-head-of-biceps-femoris.note: The only hamstring part that does not cross the hip and is not supplied by the tibial division. A classic exam question.

tibialis-anterior.origin: Lateral condyle and upper half of the lateral surface of the tibia, and the interosseous membrane.
tibialis-anterior.insertion: Medial and underside of the medial cuneiform and the base of the first metatarsal.
tibialis-anterior.actionText: Dorsiflexes the ankle and inverts the foot. It lowers the forefoot gently after heel strike.
tibialis-anterior.note: Weakness causes foot drop: a slapping foot or a high-stepping gait.

extensor-hallucis-longus.origin: Middle of the anterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-hallucis-longus.insertion: Dorsal base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
extensor-hallucis-longus.actionText: Extends the big toe and dorsiflexes the ankle.
extensor-hallucis-longus.note: Testing big-toe extension is the classic check of the L5 myotome.

extensor-digitorum-longus.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, upper three-quarters of the anterior fibula and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-digitorum-longus.originShort: Lateral tibial condyle and anterior fibula
extensor-digitorum-longus.insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5, through the extensor expansions.
extensor-digitorum-longus.actionText: Extends toes 2–5 and dorsiflexes the ankle.

fibularis-tertius.origin: Lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
fibularis-tertius.insertion: Dorsum of the base of the fifth metatarsal.
fibularis-tertius.actionText: Dorsiflexes the ankle and everts the foot.

fibularis-longus.origin: Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
fibularis-longus.insertion: Base of the first metatarsal and the medial cuneiform, reached by crossing under the sole.
fibularis-longus.actionText: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle; supports the arches of the foot.

fibularis-brevis.origin: Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
fibularis-brevis.insertion: Tuberosity on the base of the fifth metatarsal.
fibularis-brevis.actionText: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle.
fibularis-brevis.note: An inversion sprain can pull off the tuberosity it attaches to (an avulsion fracture of the fifth metatarsal).

medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius, medial head
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.origin: Posterior surface of the femur just above the medial condyle.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle and helps flex the knee. Strongest at plantarflexion when the knee is straight.
medial-head-of-gastrocnemius.note: Crosses both the knee and the ankle. The Achilles reflex tests S1.

lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius, lateral head
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle.
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
lateral-head-of-gastrocnemius.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle and helps flex the knee.

soleus.origin: Back of the head and upper fibula, the soleal line and medial border of the tibia.
soleus.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
soleus.actionText: Plantarflexes the ankle whatever the knee position. Its steady tone stops you swaying forward when standing.
soleus.note: Does not cross the knee, so it is the plantarflexor that works with the knee bent.

plantaris.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur and the oblique popliteal ligament.
plantaris.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus, alongside the calcaneal tendon.
plantaris.actionText: Weakly assists plantarflexion and knee flexion.
plantaris.note: Small and often absent; its long tendon is used for grafts.

popliteus.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle, with attachment to the lateral meniscus.
popliteus.insertion: Posterior surface of the tibia above the soleal line.
popliteus.actionText: Unlocks the fully extended knee by rotating the femur laterally on the planted tibia, then helps flex it.
popliteus.note: Called the key that unlocks the knee.

tibialis-posterior.origin: Interosseous membrane and the adjoining posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula.
tibialis-posterior.originShort: Posterior tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane
tibialis-posterior.insertion: Tuberosity of the navicular, plus the cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of metatarsals 2–4.
tibialis-posterior.actionText: Inverts the foot and plantarflexes the ankle; the main dynamic support of the medial arch.
tibialis-posterior.note: Tendon dysfunction is a common cause of adult-acquired flat foot.

flexor-digitorum-longus.origin: Posterior surface of the tibia below the soleal line.
flexor-digitorum-longus.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of toes 2–5.
flexor-digitorum-longus.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5, plantarflexes the ankle and supports the longitudinal arch.

flexor-hallucis-longus.origin: Lower two-thirds of the posterior fibula and the interosseous membrane.
flexor-hallucis-longus.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the big toe.
flexor-hallucis-longus.actionText: Flexes the big toe, plantarflexes the ankle and supports the medial arch. Gives the final push-off in walking.

extensor-digitorum-brevis.origin: Upper lateral surface of the calcaneus.

extensor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Upper lateral surface of the calcaneus.
extensor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Dorsal base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
extensor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Extends the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

abductor-hallucis.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity, the flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.
abductor-hallucis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
abductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, medial side
abductor-hallucis.actionText: Abducts and flexes the big toe; supports the medial arch.

flexor-digitorum-brevis.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and the plantar aponeurosis.
flexor-digitorum-brevis.insertion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of toes 2–5.
flexor-digitorum-brevis.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5 at the proximal interphalangeal joints.

abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Abductor digiti minimi (foot)
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.origin: Medial and lateral processes of the calcaneal tuberosity and the plantar aponeurosis.
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe.
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Abducts and flexes the fifth toe; supports the lateral arch.

quadratus-plantae.origin: Medial and lateral surfaces of the underside of the calcaneus.
quadratus-plantae.insertion: Posterolateral edge of the flexor digitorum longus tendon.
quadratus-plantae.actionText: Straightens the oblique pull of flexor digitorum longus, helping it flex the toes.

lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.name: Lumbricals (foot)
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.insertion: Medial sides of the extensor expansions of toes 2–5.
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.nerveNote: First lumbrical: medial plantar nerve. Lateral three: lateral plantar nerve
lumbrical-muscles-of-foot.actionText: Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.name: Flexor hallucis brevis, medial head
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Underside of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform.
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe, through the medial sesamoid.
medial-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Flexes the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.name: Flexor hallucis brevis, lateral head
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.origin: Underside of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform.
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe, through the lateral sesamoid.
lateral-head-of-flexor-hallucis-brevis.actionText: Flexes the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.name: Adductor hallucis, oblique head
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, lateral side
oblique-head-of-adductor-hallucis.actionText: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.name: Adductor hallucis, transverse head
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.origin: Plantar ligaments of the metatarsophalangeal joints of toes 3–5.
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of big toe, lateral side
transverse-head-of-adductor-hallucis.actionText: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Flexor digiti minimi (foot)
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe.
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Flexes the fifth toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.name: Opponens digiti minimi (foot)
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.origin: Long plantar ligament near the base of the fifth metatarsal.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.insertion: Lateral border of the fifth metatarsal.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-foot.actionText: Draws the fifth metatarsal toward the sole. Often absent and usually counted as part of flexor digiti minimi.

plantar-interossei-muscles.name: Plantar interossei
plantar-interossei-muscles.origin: Bases and medial sides of metatarsals 3–5.
plantar-interossei-muscles.insertion: Medial sides of the bases of the proximal phalanges of toes 3–5.
plantar-interossei-muscles.actionText: Adduct toes 3–5 toward the second toe (PAD) and flex the metatarsophalangeal joints.

dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.name: Dorsal interossei (foot)
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.origin: Adjacent sides of metatarsals 1–5 (four muscles, each with two heads).
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges: the first on the medial side of toe 2, the others on the lateral sides of toes 2–4.
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-foot.actionText: Abduct toes 2–4 away from the line of the second toe (DAB) and flex the metatarsophalangeal joints.

clavicular-part-of-deltoid.name: Deltoid, clavicular part
clavicular-part-of-deltoid.actionText: Flexes and medially rotates the shoulder.

acromial-part-of-deltoid.name: Deltoid, acromial part
acromial-part-of-deltoid.actionText: Abducts the shoulder after supraspinatus has started the movement (roughly beyond 15°).
acromial-part-of-deltoid.note: Axillary nerve injury (for example with a shoulder dislocation or a surgical neck fracture) weakens abduction and numbs the skin over the lower deltoid.

scapular-spinal-part-of-deltoid.name: Deltoid, spinal part
scapular-spinal-part-of-deltoid.actionText: Extends and laterally rotates the shoulder.

supraspinatus.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
supraspinatus.actionText: Starts abduction of the shoulder and holds the humeral head in the glenoid.
supraspinatus.note: The cuff tendon most often torn or impinged under the acromion.

infraspinatus.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
infraspinatus.actionText: Laterally rotates the shoulder and holds the humeral head in the glenoid.

teres-minor.origin: Middle part of the lateral border of the scapula.
teres-minor.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
teres-minor.actionText: Laterally rotates the shoulder and holds the humeral head in the glenoid.

subscapularis.origin: Subscapular fossa, on the front of the scapula.
subscapularis.actionText: Medially rotates and adducts the shoulder and holds the humeral head in the glenoid.
subscapularis.note: The only cuff muscle on the front of the scapula and the only medial rotator in the cuff.

teres-major.origin: Posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula.
teres-major.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
teres-major.actionText: Adducts, medially rotates and extends the shoulder.
teres-major.note: Not part of the rotator cuff despite its name.

long-head-of-biceps-brachii.name: Biceps brachii, long head
long-head-of-biceps-brachii.origin: Supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, with the tendon running through the shoulder joint.
long-head-of-biceps-brachii.insertion: Radial tuberosity, and through the bicipital aponeurosis into the forearm fascia.
long-head-of-biceps-brachii.actionText: Supinates the forearm (strongest with the elbow bent) and flexes the elbow; weakly flexes the shoulder.
long-head-of-biceps-brachii.note: Remember it as the muscle that puts in the corkscrew and pulls out the cork. The biceps reflex tests C5–C6.

short-head-of-biceps-brachii.name: Biceps brachii, short head
short-head-of-biceps-brachii.origin: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula.
short-head-of-biceps-brachii.insertion: Radial tuberosity, and through the bicipital aponeurosis into the forearm fascia.
short-head-of-biceps-brachii.actionText: Supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow; weakly flexes and adducts the shoulder.

brachialis.origin: Lower half of the anterior surface of the humerus.
brachialis.insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna.
brachialis.nerveNote: Musculocutaneous nerve (a small part from the radial nerve)
brachialis.actionText: Flexes the elbow in every forearm position: the workhorse elbow flexor.

coracobrachialis.origin: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula.
coracobrachialis.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus.
coracobrachialis.note: The musculocutaneous nerve passes through it.

long-head-of-triceps-brachii.name: Triceps brachii, long head
long-head-of-triceps-brachii.actionText: Extends the elbow; the long head also extends and adducts the shoulder.

lateral-head-of-triceps-brachii.name: Triceps brachii, lateral head
lateral-head-of-triceps-brachii.origin: Posterior humerus above the radial groove.

medial-head-of-triceps-brachii.name: Triceps brachii, medial head
medial-head-of-triceps-brachii.origin: Posterior humerus below the radial groove.
medial-head-of-triceps-brachii.actionText: Extends the elbow; active in all elbow extension, even against light resistance.
medial-head-of-triceps-brachii.note: The radial nerve runs in the groove between the lateral and medial heads, where a mid-shaft humerus fracture can injure it.

superficial-head-of-pronator-teres.name: Pronator teres, humeral head
superficial-head-of-pronator-teres.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (the common flexor origin).
superficial-head-of-pronator-teres.insertion: Middle of the lateral surface of the radius.
superficial-head-of-pronator-teres.actionText: Pronates the forearm and helps flex the elbow.

deep-head-of-pronator-teres.name: Pronator teres, ulnar head
deep-head-of-pronator-teres.insertion: Middle of the lateral surface of the radius.
deep-head-of-pronator-teres.note: The median nerve passes between the two heads, a site where it can be compressed.

flexor-carpi-radialis.insertion: Base of the second metacarpal (and often the third).
flexor-carpi-radialis.actionText: Flexes the wrist and deviates it toward the radial side.

palmaris-longus.insertion: Flexor retinaculum and the palmar aponeurosis.
palmaris-longus.actionText: Weakly flexes the wrist and tightens the palmar aponeurosis.
palmaris-longus.note: Absent on one or both sides in a sizeable minority of people; its tendon is a common graft source.

humeral-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris, humeral head
humeral-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.insertion: Pisiform, then the hook of the hamate and the base of the fifth metacarpal.
humeral-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.actionText: Flexes the wrist and deviates it toward the ulnar side.

ulnar-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris, ulnar head
ulnar-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.origin: Olecranon and the posterior border of the ulna.
ulnar-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.insertion: Pisiform, then the hook of the hamate and the base of the fifth metacarpal.
ulnar-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.actionText: Flexes the wrist and deviates it toward the ulnar side.
ulnar-head-of-flexor-carpi-ulnaris.note: The ulnar nerve enters the forearm between its two heads (the cubital tunnel).

humero-ulnar-head-of-flexor-digitorum-su.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis, humero-ulnar head
humero-ulnar-head-of-flexor-digitorum-su.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus, the ulnar collateral ligament and the coronoid process of the ulna.
humero-ulnar-head-of-flexor-digitorum-su.insertion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of fingers 2–5.
humero-ulnar-head-of-flexor-digitorum-su.actionText: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5, then the knuckles and the wrist.

radial-head-of-flexor-digitorum-superfic.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis, radial head
radial-head-of-flexor-digitorum-superfic.origin: Upper half of the anterior border of the radius.
radial-head-of-flexor-digitorum-superfic.insertion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of fingers 2–5.
radial-head-of-flexor-digitorum-superfic.actionText: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5, then the knuckles and the wrist.

flexor-digitorum-profundus.origin: Upper three-quarters of the anterior and medial surfaces of the ulna and the interosseous membrane.
flexor-digitorum-profundus.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of fingers 2–5.
flexor-digitorum-profundus.nerveNote: Ring and little finger parts: ulnar nerve. Index and middle finger parts: anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve
flexor-digitorum-profundus.actionText: The only muscle that flexes the distal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5; also helps flex the other finger joints and the wrist.

flexor-pollicis-longus.origin: Anterior surface of the radius and the interosseous membrane.
flexor-pollicis-longus.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
flexor-pollicis-longus.actionText: Flexes the joints of the thumb, especially the interphalangeal joint.
flexor-pollicis-longus.note: Anterior interosseous nerve injury shows as an inability to make an "OK" sign: the thumb tip and index tip cannot bend.

pronator-quadratus.origin: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the ulna.
pronator-quadratus.insertion: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the radius.
pronator-quadratus.actionText: The main pronator; holds the radius and ulna together at the wrist.

brachioradialis.origin: Upper two-thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
brachioradialis.insertion: Lateral surface of the distal radius, just above the styloid process.
brachioradialis.actionText: Flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm half-way between pronation and supination.
brachioradialis.note: An elbow flexor supplied by the radial nerve: the exception to the rule.

extensor-carpi-radialis-longus.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
extensor-carpi-radialis-longus.insertion: Dorsal base of the second metacarpal.
extensor-carpi-radialis-longus.actionText: Extends the wrist and deviates it toward the radial side; steadies the wrist when gripping.

extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (the common extensor origin).
extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.insertion: Dorsal base of the third metacarpal.
extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.nerveNote: Deep branch of the radial nerve
extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.actionText: Extends the wrist and deviates it toward the radial side.
extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.note: Its origin is the usual site of lateral epicondylalgia (tennis elbow).

extensor-digitorum.insertion: Extensor expansions of fingers 2–5, reaching the middle and distal phalanges.
extensor-digitorum.actionText: Extends fingers 2–5, mainly at the knuckles, and helps extend the wrist.

extensor-digiti-minimi.insertion: Extensor expansion of the little finger.

humeral-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris, humeral head
humeral-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.insertion: Dorsal base of the fifth metacarpal.
humeral-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.actionText: Extends the wrist and deviates it toward the ulnar side.

ulnar-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris, ulnar head
ulnar-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.insertion: Dorsal base of the fifth metacarpal.
ulnar-head-of-extensor-carpi-ulnaris.actionText: Extends the wrist and deviates it toward the ulnar side.

anconeus.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and upper posterior ulna.
anconeus.actionText: Helps triceps extend the elbow and steadies the joint.

supinator.origin: Lateral epicondyle, the radial collateral and annular ligaments, and the supinator crest of the ulna.
supinator.originShort: Lateral epicondyle and supinator crest of ulna
supinator.insertion: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the upper third of the radius.
supinator.nerveNote: Deep branch of the radial nerve
supinator.actionText: Supinates the forearm by unwinding the radius; the main supinator when the elbow is straight.
supinator.note: Wraps around the radius; the deep branch of the radial nerve passes through it.

abductor-pollicis-longus.origin: Posterior surfaces of the ulna, radius and the interosseous membrane.
abductor-pollicis-longus.actionText: Abducts the thumb and extends it at the carpometacarpal joint.
abductor-pollicis-longus.note: Its tendon and that of extensor pollicis brevis are involved in de Quervain tenosynovitis.

extensor-pollicis-brevis.origin: Posterior surface of the radius and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-pollicis-brevis.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
extensor-pollicis-brevis.actionText: Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

extensor-pollicis-longus.origin: Middle third of the posterior ulna and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-pollicis-longus.insertion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
extensor-pollicis-longus.actionText: Extends all joints of the thumb, including the interphalangeal joint.
extensor-pollicis-longus.note: Forms the ulnar border of the anatomical snuffbox.

extensor-indicis.origin: Posterior surface of the ulna and the interosseous membrane.
extensor-indicis.insertion: Extensor expansion of the index finger.

abductor-pollicis-brevis.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium.
abductor-pollicis-brevis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
abductor-pollicis-brevis.nerveNote: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
abductor-pollicis-brevis.actionText: Abducts the thumb, lifting it away from the palm.
abductor-pollicis-brevis.note: Wasting of this muscle is an early sign of carpal tunnel syndrome.

superficial-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brev.name: Flexor pollicis brevis, superficial head
superficial-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brev.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium.
superficial-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brev.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
superficial-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brev.nerveNote: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
superficial-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brev.actionText: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

deep-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brevis.name: Flexor pollicis brevis, deep head
deep-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brevis.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
deep-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brevis.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
deep-head-of-flexor-pollicis-brevis.actionText: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

opponens-pollicis.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium.
opponens-pollicis.insertion: Lateral border of the first metacarpal.
opponens-pollicis.nerveNote: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
opponens-pollicis.actionText: Opposes the thumb: rotates the first metacarpal so the thumb pad faces the finger pads.

abductor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.name: Abductor digiti minimi (hand)
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger.
abductor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve

flexor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (hand)
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.origin: Hook of the hamate and the flexor retinaculum.
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger.
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
flexor-digiti-minimi-of-hand.actionText: Flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

opponens-digiti-minimi-of-hand.name: Opponens digiti minimi (hand)
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-hand.origin: Hook of the hamate and the flexor retinaculum.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-hand.insertion: Medial border of the fifth metacarpal.
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-hand.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
opponens-digiti-minimi-of-hand.actionText: Draws the fifth metacarpal forward and rotates it to meet the thumb.

oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.name: Adductor pollicis, oblique head
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.origin: Bases of the second and third metacarpals and the capitate.
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of thumb, medial side
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.actionText: Adducts the thumb toward the palm; powers a key grip.
oblique-head-of-adductor-pollicis.note: Weakness shows as Froment's sign: the thumb tip bends to pinch a sheet of paper.

transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.name: Adductor pollicis, transverse head
transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.origin: Anterior surface of the shaft of the third metacarpal.
transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.insertionShort: Proximal phalanx of thumb, medial side
transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
transverse-head-of-adductor-pollicis.actionText: Adducts the thumb toward the palm.

lumbrical-muscles-of-hand.name: Lumbricals (hand)
lumbrical-muscles-of-hand.insertion: Lateral sides of the extensor expansions of fingers 2–5.
lumbrical-muscles-of-hand.nerveNote: First and second: median nerve. Third and fourth: deep branch of the ulnar nerve
lumbrical-muscles-of-hand.actionText: Flex the knuckles while extending the interphalangeal joints (the table-top position).

palmar-interossei-muscles.name: Palmar interossei
palmar-interossei-muscles.origin: Palmar surfaces of the second, fourth and fifth metacarpals.
palmar-interossei-muscles.insertion: Extensor expansions and bases of the proximal phalanges of the index, ring and little fingers.
palmar-interossei-muscles.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
palmar-interossei-muscles.actionText: Adduct the fingers toward the middle finger (PAD), and help flex the knuckles and extend the interphalangeal joints.

dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.name: Dorsal interossei (hand)
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.origin: Adjacent sides of the first to fifth metacarpals (four muscles, each with two heads).
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.insertion: Extensor expansions and bases of the proximal phalanges of fingers 2–4.
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.nerveNote: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.actionText: Abduct the fingers away from the middle finger (DAB), and help flex the knuckles and extend the interphalangeal joints.
dorsal-interossei-muscles-of-hand.note: Ulnar nerve injury leaves the hand with a clawed ring and little finger and wasting between the metacarpals.

descending-part-of-trapezius.name: Trapezius, descending (upper) part
descending-part-of-trapezius.origin: External occipital protuberance, medial superior nuchal line and the nuchal ligament.
descending-part-of-trapezius.nerveNote: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with sensory fibres from C3–C4
descending-part-of-trapezius.actionText: Elevates the scapula and rotates it upward; with the shoulder fixed, extends the head and neck and bends them to the same side.
descending-part-of-trapezius.note: Shrugging against resistance tests the accessory nerve.

transverse-part-of-trapezius.name: Trapezius, transverse (middle) part
transverse-part-of-trapezius.origin: Spinous processes of C7–T3 and the supraspinous ligaments.
transverse-part-of-trapezius.insertion: Acromion and the spine of the scapula.
transverse-part-of-trapezius.nerveNote: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with sensory fibres from C3–C4
transverse-part-of-trapezius.actionText: Retracts the scapula (pulls it toward the spine).

ascending-part-of-trapezius.name: Trapezius, ascending (lower) part
ascending-part-of-trapezius.insertion: Medial end of the spine of the scapula.
ascending-part-of-trapezius.nerveNote: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with sensory fibres from C3–C4
ascending-part-of-trapezius.actionText: Depresses the scapula and, with the upper part, rotates it upward so the arm can go overhead.

latissimus-dorsi.origin: Spinous processes of T7–T12, the thoracolumbar fascia, the iliac crest and the lower three or four ribs.
latissimus-dorsi.originShort: Lower thoracic spine, thoracolumbar fascia and iliac crest
latissimus-dorsi.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
latissimus-dorsi.actionText: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the shoulder; pulls the body up toward the arms (climbing, pull-ups) and helps push up from a chair.
latissimus-dorsi.note: Important for transfers and wheelchair propulsion after spinal cord injury.

levator-scapulae.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C1–C4.
levator-scapulae.insertion: Medial border of the scapula, from the superior angle to the spine.
levator-scapulae.nerveNote: Dorsal scapular nerve, plus branches of C3–C4
levator-scapulae.actionText: Elevates the scapula and tilts its glenoid down; with the scapula fixed, bends the neck to the same side.

rhomboid-major.insertion: Medial border of the scapula below the spine.
rhomboid-major.actionText: Retracts the scapula, rotates its glenoid down and fixes it against the chest wall.

rhomboid-minor.origin: Nuchal ligament and the spinous processes of C7–T1.
rhomboid-minor.insertion: Medial border of the scapula at the level of the spine.
rhomboid-minor.actionText: Retracts the scapula and rotates its glenoid down.

serratus-posterior-superior.origin: Nuchal ligament and the spinous processes of C7–T3.
serratus-posterior-superior.actionText: Thought to elevate the upper ribs; its role in breathing is uncertain and it may mainly provide position sense.

serratus-posterior-inferior.actionText: Thought to pull the lower ribs down; like the superior muscle, its role is uncertain.

splenius-capitis.origin: Lower half of the nuchal ligament and the spinous processes of C7–T3.
splenius-capitis.insertion: Mastoid process and the lateral superior nuchal line.
splenius-capitis.nerveNote: Posterior rami of the middle cervical nerves
splenius-capitis.actionText: Both sides together extend the head and neck. One side bends the neck to that side and turns the face toward it.

splenius-colli.nerveNote: Posterior rami of the lower cervical nerves
splenius-colli.actionText: Extends the neck; one side bends and turns the neck toward that side.

iliocostalis-lumborum.origin: Common erector spinae tendon from the iliac crest, sacrum and lumbar spinous processes.
iliocostalis-lumborum.insertion: Angles of the lower six or seven ribs.
iliocostalis-lumborum.actionText: Extends the lumbar spine; one side bends the trunk to that side.

iliocostalis-thoracis.origin: Angles of the lower six ribs.
iliocostalis-thoracis.insertion: Angles of the upper six ribs and the transverse process of C7.
iliocostalis-thoracis.actionText: Extends the thoracic spine; one side bends it to that side.

iliocostalis-colli.roots: Posterior rami, cervical and upper thoracic
iliocostalis-colli.actionText: Extends the neck; one side bends it to that side.

longissimus-thoracis.origin: Common erector spinae tendon and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae.
longissimus-thoracis.insertion: Transverse processes of the thoracic vertebrae and the ribs between their tubercles and angles.
longissimus-thoracis.actionText: Extends the thoracic and lumbar spine; one side bends the trunk to that side.

longissimus-colli.actionText: Extends the neck; one side bends it to that side.

longissimus-capitis.origin: Transverse processes of T1–T5 and the articular processes of C4–C7.
longissimus-capitis.originShort: Upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae
longissimus-capitis.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone.
longissimus-capitis.actionText: Extends the head; one side bends the head to that side and turns the face toward it.

spinalis-thoracis.insertion: Spinous processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae (roughly T1–T8).

spinalis-colli.origin: Nuchal ligament and the spinous processes of C7–T2.
spinalis-colli.actionText: Extends the neck. Often small or absent.

spinalis-capitis.insertion: Occipital bone, blending with semispinalis capitis.

semispinalis-thoracis.actionText: Extends the upper thoracic spine; one side rotates it toward the opposite side.

semispinalis-colli.actionText: Extends the neck; one side rotates it toward the opposite side.

multifidus-lumborum.origin: Back of the sacrum, the posterior superior iliac spine and the mammillary processes of the lumbar vertebrae.
multifidus-lumborum.insertion: Spinous processes two to four levels above.
multifidus-lumborum.actionText: Stabilises each lumbar segment; extends the spine and helps rotate it toward the opposite side.
multifidus-lumborum.note: Thickest in the lumbar region; often weak and wasted in people with low back pain, a target of motor-control exercise.

multifidus-thoracis.origin: Transverse processes of the thoracic vertebrae.
multifidus-thoracis.insertion: Spinous processes two to four levels above.
multifidus-thoracis.actionText: Stabilises the thoracic segments; extends the spine and helps rotate it toward the opposite side.

multifidus-colli.insertion: Spinous processes two to four levels above, up to C2.
multifidus-colli.actionText: Stabilises the cervical segments; extends the neck and helps rotate it toward the opposite side.

rotatores.origin: Transverse processes, best developed in the thoracic region.
rotatores.insertion: Lamina or spinous process one or two levels above.
rotatores.insertionShort: Lamina one or two levels above
rotatores.actionText: Rotate the vertebra above toward the opposite side; probably most important as position sensors.

interspinales-colli-muscles.name: Interspinales (cervical)
interspinales-colli-muscles.origin: Upper surface of a spinous process.
interspinales-colli-muscles.insertion: Lower surface of the spinous process above.
interspinales-colli-muscles.actionText: Help extend the neck and sense its position.

interspinales-thoracis-muscles.name: Interspinales (thoracic)
interspinales-thoracis-muscles.origin: Upper surface of a spinous process (only at the top and bottom of the thoracic spine).
interspinales-thoracis-muscles.insertion: Lower surface of the spinous process above.
interspinales-thoracis-muscles.actionText: Help extend the spine and sense its position.

interspinales-lumborum-muscles.name: Interspinales (lumbar)
interspinales-lumborum-muscles.origin: Upper surface of a lumbar spinous process.
interspinales-lumborum-muscles.insertion: Lower surface of the spinous process above.
interspinales-lumborum-muscles.actionText: Help extend the lumbar spine and sense its position.

dorsal-parts-of-lateral-intertransversar.name: Intertransversarii, lumbar (dorsal parts)
dorsal-parts-of-lateral-intertransversar.origin: Accessory process of a lumbar vertebra.
dorsal-parts-of-lateral-intertransversar.insertion: Mammillary process of the vertebra above.
dorsal-parts-of-lateral-intertransversar.actionText: Help bend the lumbar spine to the same side and stabilise it.

ventral-parts-of-lateral-intertransversa.name: Intertransversarii, lumbar (ventral parts)
ventral-parts-of-lateral-intertransversa.origin: Transverse process of a lumbar vertebra.
ventral-parts-of-lateral-intertransversa.insertion: Transverse process of the vertebra above.
ventral-parts-of-lateral-intertransversa.nerveNote: Anterior rami of the lumbar nerves
ventral-parts-of-lateral-intertransversa.actionText: Help bend the lumbar spine to the same side and stabilise it.

rectus-posterior-major-capitis.name: Rectus capitis posterior major
rectus-posterior-major-capitis.insertion: Lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
rectus-posterior-major-capitis.actionText: Extends the head and turns the face toward the same side.

rectus-posterior-minor-capitis.name: Rectus capitis posterior minor
rectus-posterior-minor-capitis.insertion: Medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone.

obliquus-inferior-capitis.name: Obliquus capitis inferior
obliquus-inferior-capitis.actionText: Rotates the atlas, and so the head, toward the same side.
obliquus-inferior-capitis.note: The only 'capitis' muscle that does not attach to the skull.

obliquus-superior-capitis.name: Obliquus capitis superior
obliquus-superior-capitis.insertion: Occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines.
obliquus-superior-capitis.actionText: Extends the head and bends it to the same side.

clavicular-head-of-pectoralis-major.name: Pectoralis major, clavicular head
clavicular-head-of-pectoralis-major.origin: Anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle.
clavicular-head-of-pectoralis-major.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
clavicular-head-of-pectoralis-major.nerveNote: Lateral and medial pectoral nerves (mainly lateral for this head)
clavicular-head-of-pectoralis-major.actionText: Flexes the shoulder from extension to about shoulder height, and adducts and medially rotates it.

sternocostal-head-of-pectoralis-major.name: Pectoralis major, sternocostal head
sternocostal-head-of-pectoralis-major.origin: Anterior surface of the sternum and the upper six costal cartilages.
sternocostal-head-of-pectoralis-major.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
sternocostal-head-of-pectoralis-major.actionText: Adducts and medially rotates the shoulder, and extends it from a flexed position.
sternocostal-head-of-pectoralis-major.note: The two heads work against each other in the sagittal plane: the clavicular head flexes, the sternocostal head extends from flexion.

abdominal-part-of-pectoralis-major.name: Pectoralis major, abdominal part
abdominal-part-of-pectoralis-major.origin: Aponeurosis of the external oblique (and the upper rectus sheath).
abdominal-part-of-pectoralis-major.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
abdominal-part-of-pectoralis-major.actionText: Adducts the shoulder and pulls the raised arm down and forward.

pectoralis-minor.insertion: Medial border and upper surface of the coracoid process.
pectoralis-minor.actionText: Depresses and protracts the scapula and holds it against the chest wall; with the scapula fixed, helps lift the ribs in forced inspiration.
pectoralis-minor.note: A tight pectoralis minor tilts the scapula forward, a common finding in rounded-shoulder posture.

subclavius.origin: Junction of the first rib and its costal cartilage.
subclavius.insertion: Underside of the middle third of the clavicle.

serratus-anterior.origin: Outer surfaces of the upper eight or nine ribs.
serratus-anterior.insertion: Anterior surface of the medial border of the scapula.
serratus-anterior.actionText: Protracts the scapula (punching, reaching) and holds it against the chest wall; its lower fibres rotate it upward so the arm can be raised overhead.
serratus-anterior.note: Long thoracic nerve injury makes the medial border of the scapula lift off the chest when pushing against a wall (winged scapula).

external-intercostal-muscles.name: External intercostals
external-intercostal-muscles.insertion: Upper border of the rib below; fibres run down and forward.
external-intercostal-muscles.actionText: Elevate the ribs in inspiration and keep the intercostal spaces from bulging or sinking.

internal-intercostal-muscles.name: Internal intercostals
internal-intercostal-muscles.origin: Lower border of each rib and costal cartilage.
internal-intercostal-muscles.insertion: Upper border of the rib below; fibres run down and back.
internal-intercostal-muscles.actionText: The parts between the bony ribs depress the ribs in forced expiration; the parts between the cartilages help elevate them.

innermost-intercostal-muscles.name: Innermost intercostals
innermost-intercostal-muscles.origin: Inner surface of the lower border of each rib.
innermost-intercostal-muscles.insertion: Inner surface of the upper border of the rib below.
innermost-intercostal-muscles.actionText: Probably act with the internal intercostals. The intercostal nerve and vessels run between them and the internal layer.

transversus-thoracis.origin: Posterior surface of the lower sternum and the xiphoid process.
transversus-thoracis.actionText: Weakly depresses the ribs and costal cartilages.

levatores-breves-costarum.name: Levatores costarum breves
levatores-breves-costarum.origin: Tips of the transverse processes of C7–T11.
levatores-breves-costarum.insertion: The rib immediately below, between its tubercle and angle.
levatores-breves-costarum.actionText: Elevate the ribs and help bend the spine to the same side.

levatores-longi-costarum.name: Levatores costarum longi
levatores-longi-costarum.origin: Tips of the transverse processes of the lower thoracic vertebrae.
levatores-longi-costarum.insertion: The second rib below, between its tubercle and angle.
levatores-longi-costarum.actionText: Elevate the ribs and help bend the spine to the same side.

diaphragm.origin: Xiphoid process, the inner surfaces of the lower six costal cartilages and ribs, and the bodies of L1–L3 (the crura) with the arcuate ligaments.
diaphragm.actionText: The main muscle of inspiration: contracting pulls the dome down and enlarges the chest. Also raises abdominal pressure for coughing, lifting and childbirth.
diaphragm.note: "C3, 4 and 5 keep the diaphragm alive": a spinal cord injury at or above C3 stops independent breathing.

rectus-abdominis.origin: Pubic symphysis and the pubic crest.
rectus-abdominis.actionText: Flexes the trunk (mainly the lumbar spine), tilts the pelvis backward and compresses the abdomen.
rectus-abdominis.note: Its tendinous intersections give the 'six-pack' look. A separation of the two sides at the linea alba is diastasis recti.

pyramidalis.origin: Front of the body of the pubis and the pubic symphysis.
pyramidalis.insertion: Linea alba, about half-way to the umbilicus.
pyramidalis.actionText: Tenses the linea alba. Small and absent in some people.

external-abdominal-oblique.name: External oblique
external-abdominal-oblique.insertion: Linea alba, the pubic tubercle and the anterior half of the iliac crest; its lower edge forms the inguinal ligament.
external-abdominal-oblique.insertionShort: Iliac crest, pubic tubercle and linea alba
external-abdominal-oblique.nerveNote: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11) and the subcostal nerve (T12)
external-abdominal-oblique.actionText: Compresses the abdomen. Both sides flex the trunk; the right side bends the trunk to the right and rotates it to the left (to the opposite side).
external-abdominal-oblique.note: Fibres run like hands in your front pockets.

internal-abdominal-oblique.name: Internal oblique
internal-abdominal-oblique.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, the anterior two-thirds of the iliac crest and the lateral part of the inguinal ligament.
internal-abdominal-oblique.insertion: Lower borders of ribs 10–12, the linea alba, and the pubis through the conjoint tendon.
internal-abdominal-oblique.nerveNote: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11), subcostal nerve (T12) and the first lumbar nerve
internal-abdominal-oblique.actionText: Compresses the abdomen. Both sides flex the trunk; the right side bends the trunk to the right and rotates it to the right (to the same side).
internal-abdominal-oblique.note: Works with the opposite external oblique to rotate the trunk.

transversus-abdominis.origin: Inner surfaces of costal cartilages 7–12, the thoracolumbar fascia, the iliac crest and the lateral inguinal ligament.
transversus-abdominis.originShort: Iliac crest, thoracolumbar fascia and lower costal cartilages
transversus-abdominis.insertion: Linea alba, and the pubis through the conjoint tendon.
transversus-abdominis.nerveNote: Thoracoabdominal nerves (T7–T11), subcostal nerve (T12) and the first lumbar nerve
transversus-abdominis.actionText: Compresses the abdomen like a corset and tensions the thoracolumbar fascia; switches on before limb movement to stiffen the trunk.
transversus-abdominis.note: The deepest abdominal muscle and a focus of core-stability training.

quadratus-lumborum.origin: Posterior iliac crest and the iliolumbar ligament.
quadratus-lumborum.insertion: Lower border of the twelfth rib and the transverse processes of L1–L4.
quadratus-lumborum.insertionShort: Twelfth rib and lumbar transverse processes
quadratus-lumborum.actionText: One side bends the trunk to that side or hitches the pelvis up on that side; both sides extend the lumbar spine and fix the twelfth rib during inspiration.

pubococcygeus.origin: Back of the body of the pubis and the front of the tendinous arch of levator ani.
pubococcygeus.insertion: Perineal body, anococcygeal body and coccyx.
pubococcygeus.actionText: Supports the pelvic organs, resists rises in abdominal pressure and helps maintain continence.
pubococcygeus.note: Part of levator ani; the main target of pelvic floor (Kegel) training.

pubo-analis.name: Puborectalis (pubo-analis)
pubo-analis.origin: Back of the body of the pubis.
pubo-analis.insertion: Loops behind the anorectal junction to join the muscle of the other side.
pubo-analis.actionText: Pulls the anorectal junction forward, keeping the anorectal angle that is essential for faecal continence; relaxes to allow defecation.

iliococcygeus.origin: Tendinous arch of levator ani and the ischial spine.
iliococcygeus.actionText: Forms the back part of the pelvic floor and supports the pelvic organs.

coccygeus.name: Coccygeus (ischiococcygeus)
coccygeus.insertion: Lower end of the sacrum and the coccyx.
coccygeus.nerveNote: Branches of the anterior rami of S3–S4
coccygeus.actionText: Completes the back of the pelvic floor, supports the pelvic organs and pulls the coccyx forward.

frontalis.name: Frontalis (frontal belly of occipitofrontalis)
frontalis.insertion: Skin and fascia of the forehead and eyebrows.
frontalis.actionText: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead (surprise).
frontalis.note: Has no bony attachment of its own: it moves skin over the frontal bone.

occipitalis.name: Occipitalis (occipital belly of occipitofrontalis)
occipitalis.origin: Lateral two-thirds of the superior nuchal line and the mastoid process.

temporoparietalis.insertion: Lateral border of the epicranial aponeurosis.
temporoparietalis.actionText: Tightens the scalp and slightly raises the ear. Variable in size.

orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.name: Orbicularis oculi, orbital part
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.origin: Nasal part of the frontal bone, frontal process of the maxilla and the medial palpebral ligament.
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.insertion: Skin around the orbit, in a ring back to the origin.
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and zygomatic branches
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.actionText: Closes the eyelids tightly (squeezing the eyes shut, squinting).
orbital-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.note: Inability to close the eye on one side is a key sign of facial nerve palsy (for example Bell's palsy).

palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.name: Orbicularis oculi, palpebral part
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.insertion: Lateral palpebral raphe, within the eyelids.
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and zygomatic branches
palpebral-part-of-orbicularis-oculi.actionText: Closes the eyelids gently, as in blinking and sleep.

corrugator-supercilii.origin: Medial end of the superciliary arch of the frontal bone.
corrugator-supercilii.insertion: Skin above the middle of the eyebrow.
corrugator-supercilii.actionText: Draws the eyebrows down and together, making vertical frown lines.

procerus.origin: Fascia over the nasal bone and upper nasal cartilage.
procerus.nerveNote: Facial nerve, temporal and buccal branches
procerus.actionText: Pulls the inner eyebrows down and wrinkles the bridge of the nose.

nasalis.origin: Maxilla above the incisor and canine teeth.
nasalis.insertion: Nasal cartilages and the skin of the nose.
nasalis.actionText: Its transverse part narrows the nostrils; its alar part flares them.

depressor-septi-nasi.origin: Incisive fossa of the maxilla, above the central incisor.
depressor-septi-nasi.insertion: Mobile part of the nasal septum.
depressor-septi-nasi.actionText: Pulls the nasal septum down and narrows the nostrils.

levator-nasolabialis.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
levator-nasolabialis.insertion: Alar cartilage of the nose and the upper lip.
levator-nasolabialis.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-nasolabialis.actionText: Elevates the upper lip and flares the nostril (a snarl).

orbicularis-oris.origin: Maxilla and mandible near the midline, and the modiolus at each corner of the mouth.
orbicularis-oris.insertion: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips.
orbicularis-oris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, buccal and marginal mandibular branches
orbicularis-oris.actionText: Closes the lips and purses or protrudes them (whistling, kissing).

bucinator.name: Buccinator
bucinator.origin: Alveolar processes of the maxilla and mandible opposite the molars, and the pterygomandibular raphe.
bucinator.insertion: Angle of the mouth, blending with orbicularis oris.
bucinator.actionText: Presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food between them when chewing; helps blow and whistle.
bucinator.note: Supplied by the facial nerve, not by the buccal branch of the trigeminal nerve (which only carries sensation).

zygomaticus-major.origin: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone.
zygomaticus-major.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
zygomaticus-major.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
zygomaticus-major.actionText: Draws the angle of the mouth up and out: the smiling muscle.

zygomaticus-minor.origin: Anterior surface of the zygomatic bone.
zygomaticus-minor.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches

levator-labii-superioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip.
levator-labii-superioris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-labii-superioris.actionText: Elevates and everts the upper lip.

levator-anguli-oris.origin: Canine fossa of the maxilla, below the infraorbital foramen.
levator-anguli-oris.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
levator-anguli-oris.nerveNote: Facial nerve, zygomatic and buccal branches
levator-anguli-oris.actionText: Elevates the angle of the mouth.

risorius.origin: Parotid fascia and the skin over the masseter.
risorius.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
risorius.actionText: Pulls the angle of the mouth straight out to the side (a grimace).

depressor-anguli-oris.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
depressor-anguli-oris.actionText: Pulls the angle of the mouth down (frowning, sadness).

depressor-labii-inferioris.insertion: Skin and muscle of the lower lip.
depressor-labii-inferioris.actionText: Pulls the lower lip down and to the side.

mentalis.actionText: Raises and protrudes the lower lip and wrinkles the chin (pouting).

superficial-part-of-masseter.name: Masseter, superficial part
superficial-part-of-masseter.origin: Lower border of the front two-thirds of the zygomatic arch and the zygomatic process of the maxilla.
superficial-part-of-masseter.insertion: Angle and lower lateral surface of the ramus of the mandible.
superficial-part-of-masseter.nerveNote: Masseteric nerve, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)
superficial-part-of-masseter.actionText: Elevates the mandible (closes the jaw) and helps protrude it.
superficial-part-of-masseter.note: Clench your teeth and you can feel it bulge at the angle of the jaw.

deep-part-of-masseter.name: Masseter, deep part
deep-part-of-masseter.origin: Inner surface and back third of the zygomatic arch.
deep-part-of-masseter.insertion: Upper lateral ramus and the coronoid process of the mandible.
deep-part-of-masseter.actionText: Elevates the mandible and helps retract it.

temporalis.origin: Floor of the temporal fossa and the deep surface of the temporal fascia.
temporalis.insertion: Coronoid process and the front of the ramus of the mandible.
temporalis.nerveNote: Deep temporal nerves, from CN V3
temporalis.actionText: Elevates the mandible; its horizontal back fibres retract it.

medial-pterygoid.origin: Medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate (sphenoid), the palatine bone and the tuberosity of the maxilla.
medial-pterygoid.insertion: Medial surface of the ramus of the mandible near the angle.
medial-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to medial pterygoid, from CN V3
medial-pterygoid.actionText: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; acting with the opposite side's lateral pterygoid it grinds the jaw from side to side.

superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.name: Lateral pterygoid, superior head
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.origin: Infratemporal surface of the greater wing of the sphenoid.
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.insertion: Articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint and the neck of the mandible.
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from CN V3
superior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.actionText: Steadies the disc and condyle as the jaw closes; helps protrude the mandible.

inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.name: Lateral pterygoid, inferior head
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.insertion: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the mandible.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.nerveNote: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from CN V3
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.actionText: Pulls the condyle forward to protrude the mandible and to open the mouth wide; one side swings the jaw to the opposite side.
inferior-head-of-lateral-pterygoid.note: The only muscle of mastication that helps open the jaw.

lateral-rectus.origin: Common tendinous ring at the back of the orbit.
lateral-rectus.insertion: Sclera on the lateral side of the eyeball.
lateral-rectus.note: Abducens palsy leaves the eye turned inward and causes double vision on looking to that side.

superior-oblique.origin: Body of the sphenoid above the optic canal.
superior-oblique.insertion: Sclera at the back of the upper lateral eyeball, after passing through the trochlea.
superior-oblique.actionText: Depresses the eye when it is turned inward (looking down toward the nose), and rotates it inward (intorsion).
superior-oblique.note: Trochlear palsy makes walking downstairs and reading difficult; patients tilt the head away from the affected side.

genioglossus.origin: Superior mental spine on the inner surface of the mandible.
genioglossus.insertion: Whole length of the tongue's underside and the body of the hyoid.
genioglossus.actionText: Protrudes the tongue and depresses its centre.
genioglossus.note: With a hypoglossal nerve lesion, the protruded tongue points toward the weak side.

hyoglossus.origin: Body and greater horn of the hyoid.
hyoglossus.insertion: Side and underside of the tongue.

platysma.origin: Fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid.
platysma.insertion: Lower border of the mandible, the skin of the lower face and the angle of the mouth.
platysma.actionText: Tenses the skin of the neck and draws the corners of the mouth and the mandible down (a strained grimace).

sternocleidomastoid.origin: Sternal head: front of the manubrium. Clavicular head: upper surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
sternocleidomastoid.insertion: Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.
sternocleidomastoid.nerveNote: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with proprioceptive fibres from C2–C3
sternocleidomastoid.actionText: One side bends the neck to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side. Both sides flex the neck (and extend the head on the neck) and lift the sternum in forced inspiration.
sternocleidomastoid.note: The right SCM turns the face to the left. A shortened SCM in infants causes torticollis.

anterior-belly-of-digastric.name: Digastric, anterior belly
anterior-belly-of-digastric.origin: Digastric fossa on the inner lower border of the mandible.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid by a fibrous sling.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.nerveNote: Nerve to mylohyoid, from CN V3
anterior-belly-of-digastric.actionText: Elevates the hyoid; with the hyoid fixed, opens the jaw.
anterior-belly-of-digastric.note: Its two bellies have different nerves because they develop from different pharyngeal arches.

posterior-belly-of-digastric.name: Digastric, posterior belly
posterior-belly-of-digastric.origin: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone.
posterior-belly-of-digastric.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid by a fibrous sling.
posterior-belly-of-digastric.actionText: Elevates and retracts the hyoid; helps open the jaw.

stylohyoid.origin: Styloid process of the temporal bone.
stylohyoid.actionText: Elevates and retracts the hyoid, lengthening the floor of the mouth during swallowing.

mylohyoid.origin: Mylohyoid line on the inner surface of the mandible.
mylohyoid.insertion: Midline raphe and the body of the hyoid.
mylohyoid.nerveNote: Nerve to mylohyoid, from CN V3
mylohyoid.actionText: Forms the floor of the mouth; elevates the hyoid, floor of the mouth and tongue in swallowing; helps open the jaw.

geniohyoid.origin: Inferior mental spine of the mandible.
geniohyoid.actionText: Pulls the hyoid up and forward; with the hyoid fixed, helps open the jaw.

sternohyoid.origin: Back of the manubrium and the medial end of the clavicle.

omohyoid.origin: Upper border of the scapula near the suprascapular notch.
omohyoid.insertion: Lower border of the body of the hyoid.
omohyoid.actionText: Depresses and steadies the hyoid; has two bellies joined by an intermediate tendon tethered to the clavicle.

sternothyroid.insertion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
sternothyroid.actionText: Depresses the larynx (and with it the hyoid).

thyrohyoid.origin: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
thyrohyoid.insertion: Lower border of the body and greater horn of the hyoid.
thyrohyoid.actionText: Depresses the hyoid; with the hyoid fixed, raises the larynx during swallowing.

scalenus-anterior.name: Anterior scalene
scalenus-anterior.origin: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6.
scalenus-anterior.insertion: Scalene tubercle of the first rib.
scalenus-anterior.actionText: Elevates the first rib in forced inspiration; bends the neck to the same side and helps flex it.
scalenus-anterior.note: Tight scalenes can compress the brachial plexus (thoracic outlet syndrome).

scalenus-medius.name: Middle scalene
scalenus-medius.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C7.
scalenus-medius.insertion: Upper surface of the first rib behind the groove for the subclavian artery.
scalenus-medius.actionText: Elevates the first rib and bends the neck to the same side.

scalenus-posterior.name: Posterior scalene
scalenus-posterior.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C4–C6.
scalenus-posterior.insertion: Outer surface of the second rib.
scalenus-posterior.actionText: Elevates the second rib and bends the neck to the same side.

longus-colli.origin: Bodies of C5–T3 and the transverse processes of C3–C5.
longus-colli.insertion: Anterior tubercle of the atlas, the bodies of C2–C4 and the transverse processes of C5–C6.
longus-colli.actionText: Flexes the neck and helps bend and rotate it; important for holding the cervical spine stable.
longus-colli.note: A deep neck flexor often retrained after whiplash and in neck pain (the cranio-cervical flexion test).

longus-capitis.origin: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6.
longus-capitis.insertion: Basilar part of the occipital bone.
longus-capitis.actionText: Flexes the head on the neck.

rectus-anterior-capitis.name: Rectus capitis anterior
rectus-anterior-capitis.origin: Front of the lateral mass of the atlas.
rectus-anterior-capitis.insertion: Base of the occipital bone in front of the condyle.
rectus-anterior-capitis.actionText: Flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

rectus-lateralis-capitis.name: Rectus capitis lateralis
rectus-lateralis-capitis.insertion: Jugular process of the occipital bone.
rectus-lateralis-capitis.actionText: Bends the head to the same side and steadies it.

trunkFlex:+.note: From lying down, psoas and iliacus lift the trunk once the abdominals have curled the spine.
